text: Revised collaboration agreement (2026-09-25, about 20:12 CEST), from the human's own messages. The human asked: 'Can you ensure that the story is fully finished? so you iterate on a finished story? And make it longer? I want it to produce a nice pdf too.' Asked two questions, the human chose: about 16,000 words (still twelve parts, about 1,350 words each), and to work straight through to a complete draft of all twelve parts before checking in, instead of stopping every fifteen minutes. The human then added: 'The story needs to be inside the graph, nothing written outside of it.' So: every draft, review, revision and plan lives in the story graph; prose is drafted directly into draft records, reviewed and committed there, and revised only through graph edits; novel.md and the PDF are renders of the graph, never separately edited; the JSON files in inputs/ exist only because the relay takes its arguments from files and are not a manuscript. After the full draft: iterate on the finished story, then produce a nice PDF from the rendered text, then report. These are human decisions; they supersede the length and the round rhythm of author.agreement, which otherwise stands.

involvement.checkIn: after the complete draft, then after iteration and the PDF

data.storyLocation: inside the story graph only; renders are exports
deliverables: complete twelve-part draft committed in the graph
a nice PDF made from the rendered text
